questions.markdown:
A light string ABCDE whose extremity A is fixed, has weights $W_1$ and $W_2$ attached to it at B and C. It passes round a small frictionless pulley (neglect the weight of pulley) at D carrying a weight of $300\,\text{N}$ at the free end E as shown in the figure. If in the equilibrium position, BC is horizontal, find

(i) Tension in the portions AB, BC and CD of the string and
(ii) Magnitudes of $W_1$ and $W_2$.

diagrams.caption: Light string ABCDE over a frictionless pulley at D, with weights W1 at B, W2 at C, and 300 N hanging at E. (original source region)

questions.markdown: Explain the Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) and the Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (SEER) highlighting the differences between their operating conditions.

Calculate the stress developed in each section of the composite bar consisting of steel, aluminum, and bronze sections rigidly connected as shown in the figure. Also, determine the deformation of each section and the overall change in length of the bar.

Given:
$E_{\text{bronze}} = 100\,\text{GPa}$, $E_{\text{aluminium}} = 70\,\text{GPa}$, $E_{\text{steel}} = 200\,\text{GPa}$.
Cross sectional area and length of Aluminum section: $600\,\text{mm}^2$ and $800\,\text{mm}$ respectively.
Cross sectional area and length of Steel section: $1000\,\text{mm}^2$ and $1200\,\text{mm}$ respectively.
Cross sectional area and length of Bronze section: $1500\,\text{mm}^2$ and $1400\,\text{mm}$ respectively.

diagrams.caption: Composite bar with Aluminum, Steel and Bronze sections and applied axial forces of 4 kN, 12 kN, 8 kN and 16 kN. (original source region)

questions.markdown:
A steel bar $40\,\text{mm} \times 40\,\text{mm}$ in cross-section and $140\,\text{mm}$ length is subjected to an axial compressive load of $250\,\text{kN}$ longitudinally.

i) Determine the deformation in length of the bar if the lateral strain is fully prevented.
ii) Determine the deformation in length of the bar if only one-third of the lateral strain is prevented.
Take Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio of steel bar as $205\,\text{GPa}$ and $0.3$ respectively.
Derive the relationship between young's modulus $(E)$ and modulus of rigidity $(G)$ for a deformable body.

A mild steel bar of $30\,\text{mm}$ diameter, $250\,\text{mm}$ length, has an extension of $0.20\,\text{mm}$ under a load of $85\,\text{kN}$. The load at the elastic limit is $170\,\text{kN}$, and the ultimate load is $280\,\text{kN}$. The total extension is $45\,\text{mm}$ and diameter at the fracture is $19.5\,\text{mm}$. Calculate the elastic modulus of the material, stress at the elastic limit, ultimate strength of the material, percentage elongation and percentage reduction in cross-sectional area.

A bar $25\,\text{mm}$ in diameter and $500\,\text{mm}$ in length is acted upon by an axial load of $40\,\text{kN}$. The elongation of the bar and change in diameter are measured as $0.175\,\text{mm}$ and $0.0041\,\text{mm}$, respectively. Calculate Poisson's ratio and three moduli. Also, determine the allowable stress if a factor of safety is $1.5$.
Explain briefly five types of displacement sensors.

Explain the working mechanisms of

i) Strain gauge
ii) pH sensor
